title: Customer review metric definitions and renewal ops table
content:
Purpose:
This working doc defines the canonical metric definitions we should use in customer-facing review decks (customer reviews / exec check-ins / renewal conversations). It also includes a compact KPI table format and an operational action matrix so CS and Solutions can quickly assess renewal risk from service-level signals.

Audience:
- Customer Success Managers (CSMs)
- Solutions Engineering / Renewals 
- Account Execs for escalation context
- Product & Observability partners (for metric instrumentation)

Scope / assumptions:
- Focused on production inference signals: latency, uptime, cost/token, cache hit rate.
- Metrics are computed over rolling 7d and 30d windows for trend and stability.
- We assume per-customer routing and tagging exists (customer_id, route, model_variant). If not, mark as instrumentation debt.

Quick summary definitions (plain language):
- Median p95 latency (ms): The 95th percentile per-request server-side latency for text-generation endpoints, measured at edge exit point (after routing + queuing) excluding gateway retries. Report both p50 and p95; p95 is primary for SLAs.
- Uptime (availability %): Percentage of successful inference responses (2xx) vs total attempts, excluding planned maintenance windows. Use 30d window for contractual SLAs and 7d for near-term incidents.
- Cost per token (USD/token): End-to-end unit cost allocated to the customer: GPU compute + memory + infra amortized + infra networking where measurable. We currently use a model-based estimate (cost model v1) — see linked_artifacts. 
- Cache hit rate (prefix/KV cache %): Fraction of token generation requests where prefix or KV cache served a hit that avoided full attention recompute. Measured at model-serving runtime and attributed to route+customer.

Formal calculation snippets (for instrumentation/analytics):
- p95_latency_ms = percentile(95, request_latency_ms filtered by customer_id and route) over window
- uptime_pct = (count(status=2xx) / count(total_requests_excluding_scheduled_maintenance)) * 100
- cost_per_token_usd = (sum(customer_token_cost_estimate) / sum(tokens_generated)) rounded to 6 decimals
- cache_hit_rate_pct = (sum(cache_hits) / sum(cache_lookups)) * 100

Sampling windows & why:
- 7d rolling: surface recent regressions (useful for incident -> renewal risk signalling)
- 30d rolling: stable baseline for QBRs, smoothing out bursty workloads
- Compare 7d vs 30d to detect recent degradation (delta thresholds in action matrix)

Suggested default SLO bands (customer-facing tiers, adapt per contract):
- Tier: Enterprise (SLA-backed)
  - p95 latency: target < 300ms (green), 300–500ms (amber), >500ms (red)
  - uptime: target >= 99.95% (green), 99.90%–99.95% (amber), <99.90% (red)
  - cost/token: baseline depends on model/sequence; flag if above 20% of expected estimated baseline for >7d
  - cache hit rate: target >= 45% (green), 30–45% (amber), <30% (red)
- Tier: Growth / Mid-market
  - p95 latency: < 450ms (green), 450–700ms (amber), >700ms (red)
  - uptime: >= 99.9% (green), 99.7%–99.9% (amber), <99.7% (red)
  - cost/token: flag at +30% above baseline
  - cache hit rate: >=35% green, 20–35% amber, <20% red

KPI table template (one-row per route/customer):
Columns: [customer_name, tier, route, model_variant, tokens_7d, p95_7d_ms, p95_30d_ms, uptime_30d_pct, cost_per_token_30d_usd, cache_hit_30d_pct, trend_flag, owner, renewal_risk_score]
Example row (textified):
- Acme Corp | Enterprise | /v1/generate/chat | rw-instruct-13B-q4 | 12,430,000 | 275 | 260 | 99.96 | 0.00042 | 52 | stable | Priya Nair | 8/100
Notes: trend_flag = delta(p95_7d vs p95_30d) > 10% => "degrading". renewal_risk_score is computed per algorithm below.

Renewal risk scoring (draft heuristics, numeric 0–100):
- baseline_score = 0
- add weighted penalties (higher is worse):
  - p95 latency band: amber +5, red +15
  - uptime band: amber +10, red +30
  - cost over baseline: >+20% -> +8, >+50% -> +20
  - cache hit rate falling into amber -> +6, red -> +14
  - negative trend (7d vs 30d delta > 20% for any primary metric) -> +12
  - >5 active P1/P2 incidents in 30d -> +25
  - high support volume (tickets per 100k tokens > threshold) -> +10
- cap at 100. Interpret: 0–9 low risk, 10–29 medium, 30–59 high, 60+ at-risk/expedite renewal involvement.

Operational action matrix (when you see Amber/Red):
- p95 amber for 7d (non-enterprise): CSM opens a "performance check" ticket, owner = Solutions Eng (SE) for runbook review. Notify product-observability.
- p95 red or uptime red: immediate postmortem on incidents, open cross-functional incident triage. Escalate to SRE and account exec. Prepare temporary mitigation: route to lower-latency model variant or enable aggressive caching for that route.
- Cost spike (sustained >20% above baseline for 7d): run cost investigation; check batch sizes, sampling lengths, trending prompts; recommend batching/quantization or smaller model variant. SE to produce a recommended config and estimated cost delta.
- Cache hit drop below threshold: ask infra/serving to validate cache population policy, warmup strategies, and model cache compatibility after rollout (common after model upgrades).

Playbook checklist for CSM prior to renewal meeting:
1) Pull KPI table for customer — verify p95, uptime, cost/token, cache hit for 7d/30d.
2) Run renewal_risk_score calc; if >=30, involve Solutions and SRE in pre-call.
3) Prepare 2–3 improvement suggestions (config changes, model swap, workload batching). Include estimated cost impact.
4) Document any open tickets and incident timelines and remediation plan.
5) Slide deck: single summary slide with risk score + 1 slide per action item.

Suggested queries & example PromQL-like pseudo queries (put into observability backlog):
- p95 latency by customer (7d): histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_bucket{customer_id=~"$customer"}[7d])) by (le, route, model_variant))
- uptime: sum(rate(requests_total{customer_id=~"$customer", status=~"2.."}[30d])) / sum(rate(requests_total{customer_id=~"$customer"}[30d]))
- cache hit rate: sum(rate(cache_hits{customer_id=~"$customer"}[30d])) / sum(rate(cache_lookups{customer_id=~"$customer"}[30d]))
- cost per token: (sum(rate(inf_cost_estimate_usd{customer_id=~"$customer"}[30d])) / sum(rate(tokens_emitted{customer_id=~"$customer"}[30d])))

Deck / visualization guidance:
- Summary slide: one row per route with color-coded risk band and renewal_risk_score on right. Keep wording actionable ("root cause: model upgrade increased sequence length by 2x -> cost +32%" rather than generic).
- Trend charts: show 7d vs 30d overlays and a delta percent in annotations.
- Waterfall for cost: show token volume, avg sequence length, model mix (%), and per-token compute cost to explain variance.

Instrumention & data quality checklist (known gaps):
- Ensure request tags include customer_id, route, model_variant, batch_id. Missing tags => manual attribution errors.
- Cost model: v1 uses fleet-wide amortization; add per-cluster accounting for Dedicated customers.
- Cache metrics: runtime emits cache_hits but not always tagged by route after proxy layer — engineering ticket pending.

Unresolved questions / notes to self:
- Should we normalize cost/token to a reference model (e.g., rw-instruct-13B) for easier cross-customer comparisons? Pros/cons discussed — add to product review.
- Rethink weights in renewal_risk_score after running against past 12 months of closed renewals. Need historical data mapping.
- Consider adding a customer sentiment signal from CS surveys as a modifier.

Appendix: example small-batch remediation templates for SEs (short):
- Rapid temporary mitigation: enable per-route aggressive KV/prefix caching -> expected latency improvement 20–50% depending on reuse.
- Mid-term: switch to a lower-cost quantized variant for non-critical routes -> estimated cost drop 30% but validate quality with test prompts.

References / cross-links (already included in linked_artifacts):
- Renewal playbook v2 on Confluence
- Observability metrics spec repo (ops-notebooks) PR link
- Jira to track cache tagging work: JIRA-4321

Last notes: this doc is an operational draft intended to be iterated in sync with product for baseline bands and with finance for cost model calibration. Use this as the working canonical source for CS -> SE handoffs during renewal prep until we formalize a single Confluence page.
